_comment: The §3 derivation of slice C from slice B's five evidence sources.
AUTHORED, not generated — ranking by cost/closeable/owned is a judgment, and
a script that produced one would be manufacturing the taste-based selection
§3 exists to prevent. `collect_slice_evidence.py` reads this file.

ranked_candidates.leak: the engine knows why your game did not start and will not tell you
ranked_candidates.cost: HIGHEST, because it is SILENT and §3a triples silent. The minimal game composed, booted, and sat in `HostStatus::Activating` for 600 ticks with no message: preparation validation had refused it for registering no audio fragment. Outlander's comment already recorded the gap AND its worst property — 'a good message that a headless host surfaced NOWHERE' — so a KNOWN defect sat there and the second consumer walked straight into it. Every consumer will.
ranked_candidates.closeable: YES. The validation already produces a message; nothing carries it to a place a consumer can read. A `HostStatus::Failed { reason }` arm plus a published preparation diagnostic closes it without moving code between crates.
ranked_candidates.owned: YES. The engine performs the validation, holds the reason, and drops it.

ranked_candidates.leak: a movement-only game links 19 Ambition crates it never asked for
ranked_candidates.cost: HIGH and structural. 41 crates reachable from one declared dependency; 19 are menus, persistence, cutscenes, encounters, inventory UI, portals, projectiles, LDtk, settings menus, touch input. The consumer-matrix question is now ANSWERED — yes, a small game links all of it.
ranked_candidates.closeable: UNKNOWN, and that is the finding rather than an excuse. §4 authorises a carve when a footprint cannot be reduced WITHOUT moving code. This shows the footprint is large; it does not show it is irreducible, because FEATURE-GATING HAS NOT BEEN TRIED. The closure was measured from the workspace graph, which ignores features, so it is an upper bound.
ranked_candidates.route: 3b: measurement ran, and it ROUTED THE CANDIDATE AWAY from decomposition. Closeable + Owned -> a facade-optionality slice, candidate for D.
ranked_candidates.action: queue as the first experiment of slice C, before its main work

experiment_result.finding: 39 of 39 direct `ambition_*` dependencies of the facade are UNCONDITIONAL. Zero are `optional = true`. `default = []` is cosmetic: the feature table gates behaviour flags, never the dependency edges.
experiment_result.verdict: THE CARVE TRIGGER DOES NOT FIRE.
experiment_result.why: §4 authorises an internal carve when a sentinel consumer's capability footprint cannot be reduced WITHOUT MOVING CODE BETWEEN CRATES. The footprint here is not irreducible — it has simply never been reduced. Making 19 dependency edges optional and gating their re-exports is entirely within the facade, moves no code, and is the obvious first attempt nobody has made. A decomposition argued on this evidence would have been arguing that a door is welded shut without trying the handle.
experiment_result.what_it_becomes_instead: A facade optionality slice — cheap, contained, and measurable by the same instrument. If 19 optional features still cannot shrink the closure (because the re-exports are load-bearing through `ambition_platformer2d_actor_monolith`, which carries 27 direct ambition dependencies of its own), THAT result is the carve argument — and it will name the boundary instead of guessing at one.
experiment_result.why_this_matters_beyond_the_number: This is the measurement overruling the appealing structural conclusion. 'A minimal game links 19 crates it never asked for' reads as proof that the monolith must be split, and ADR 0031 deferred exactly that split because 'the split designed today would fit today's INTERNAL topology'. One `grep optional` was the difference between an evidence-backed slice and weeks of refactor justified by a number nobody interrogated.

FOLLOW_UP_2026_07_30.measured: Of the 19 crates a movement-only game never asked for, FIFTEEN are reachable from `ambition_platformer2d_actor_monolith` ALONE: menu, persistence, cutscene, encounter, portal, projectiles, ldtk_map, settings_menu, items, dialog, sfx, audio, vfx, ui_nav, sfx_bank. Only FOUR (inventory_ui, touch_input, render, portal_presentation) come in through the facade's own direct edges.
FOLLOW_UP_2026_07_30.verdict: ⚠ THE EARLIER VERDICT IS REVERSED. §4's carve trigger DOES fire.
FOLLOW_UP_2026_07_30.why_the_first_answer_was_incomplete: The first measurement — 39 of 39 facade dependencies unconditional, zero optional — was CORRECT, and the conclusion drawn from it was not. 'Nobody has tried feature-gating' is true and says nothing about whether feature-gating would WORK. Doing the follow-up shows it cannot: making every facade edge optional removes at most 4 of 19, because a game that needs actors needs `ambition_platformer2d_actor_monolith`, and `ambition_platformer2d_actor_monolith` brings the other 15.
FOLLOW_UP_2026_07_30.so_the_footprint_IS_irreducible: §4 authorises a carve when a sentinel consumer's capability footprint cannot be reduced without moving code between crates. Fifteen unwanted crates cannot be removed by any manifest change, because they arrive through a crate every game must have. That is the condition, met and measured.
FOLLOW_UP_2026_07_30.and_it_confirms_ADR_0031s_diagnosis_exac: ADR 0031 accepted the diagnosis that `ambition_platformer2d_actor_monolith` 'owns audio, menu content, persistence compatibility, LDtk loading, session lifecycle, cutscene playback and boss orchestration alongside actor simulation' — and deferred the split because 'the split designed today would fit today's INTERNAL topology'. The fifteen crates measured here are literally that list. The diagnosis was right all along; what was missing was a CONSUMER-measured reason, which is what the campaign was built to produce and has now produced.
FOLLOW_UP_2026_07_30.what_it_does_NOT_authorise: ⚠ Still not a free hand. §4: 'Carve exactly the boundary the leak NAMES.' The leak names a specific boundary — the fifteen capability domains a movement-only game links through `ambition_platformer2d_actor_monolith` but never asked for. It does not authorise reorganising `ambition_platformer2d_actor_monolith` by its internal topology, which is the thing ADR 0031 refused. The carve is 'separate what a game must have from what it merely inherits', and the fifteen names ARE the specification.

ranked_candidates.leak: every game must register an empty audio fragment to declare silence
ranked_candidates.cost: MODERATE, every game, once. Loud once you know; invisible before — it presents as the silent hang above rather than as an audio error.
ranked_candidates.closeable: YES, the same way slice B closed the character version: make the true answer sayable on the draft rather than defaulting it silently.
ranked_candidates.route: 3b: Closeable + Owned -> rides inside slice C. It is the same leak wearing a different noun, and closing it separately would be two slices for one lesson.

ranked_candidates.leak: `ambition_platformer2d::world` is still a whole-crate re-export, so it cannot be promoted to reviewed SDK surface
ranked_candidates.cost: LOW as felt pain — the minimal game already reaches only the curated prelude. It is a BLOCKER on the ratchet reaching zero, though, which is §4's first terminal condition.
ranked_candidates.closeable: YES. Turn the facade's `pub use ambition_platformer2d_world as world` into a curated module.
ranked_candidates.route: 3b: Closeable + Owned -> slice D candidate. Deferred because it is the same shape for every domain module and doing one in isolation invents a pattern the other domains then have to match; the doctrine ADR 0031 defers to the END is exactly this.

ranked_candidates.leak: Outlander still names 14 modules — runtime 13, platformer 11, actors 10, sprite_sheet 9, characters 7
ranked_candidates.cost: HIGH by count, but the counts are gameplay and content vocabulary, not composition.
ranked_candidates.closeable: Partly, and not by one seam.
ranked_candidates.route: 3b: needs its own derivation once the domain-module pattern from the row above exists. Attacking it before that pattern is chosen would produce fourteen ad-hoc decisions.

slice_c.name: make failure legible
slice_c.one_leak: the engine validates a game's content, refuses it, and drops the reason — so a consumer sees a host that runs forever and does nothing.
why_this_and_not_the_footprint: The footprint (19 unwanted crates) is the bigger STRUCTURAL finding and it is deliberately not slice C. §4 authorises a carve only when the footprint cannot be reduced without moving code, and nobody has tried features yet. Choosing a decomposition on an unmeasured premise is the exact failure ADR 0031 rejected when it deferred the `ambition_platformer2d_actor_monolith` split: 'the split designed today would fit today's INTERNAL topology.'
So the feature experiment runs FIRST, inside slice C, as a measurement. It is cheap and it either dissolves the candidate or promotes it to the strongest carve argument the campaign has.
Meanwhile the silent-failure leak is the highest-cost CLOSEABLE one by §3a's own arithmetic, and it is the leak that already cost this campaign a false 'proven' on a consumer-matrix row.

It is also a precondition for the blind-agent gate. §4.2 requires a run that opens NO engine file; an author who cannot find out why their game will not start WILL open engine files. Closing this is how that condition becomes reachable rather than aspirational.

⚠ RESOLVED 2026-07-30, and against the interesting answer: the experiment ran and the carve trigger does NOT fire. Zero of the facade's 39 direct ambition dependencies are optional, so the footprint is not irreducible — it is unreduced. See candidate 2's `experiment_result`.
not_in_this_slice: the ambition_platformer2d_actor_monolith decomposition, and any crate move at all
curating the facade's domain modules (slice D — it needs one pattern for all domains, not one precedent)
the bevy_ggrs patch table — deferred by maintainer decision pending upstream
pack identity, namespaces, content fingerprints, the PreStartup backstop
exit_criteria_sketch: a game whose content fails validation gets a NAMED reason through the public surface, and a test asserts the reason names the missing thing;
`HostStatus` distinguishes 'still preparing' from 'refused', so a poll loop can stop instead of spinning 600 ticks;
declaring silence is a draft call, not a hand-registered fragment, and `ambition_platformer2d::audio` leaves the minimal game's baseline;
the feature-gating experiment is RECORDED with a number either way — that measurement is the deliverable even if it changes nothing;
